FINDING_ID: IM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorDiagnosis` is not a dataclass or otherwise constructible with keyword arguments in the shown artifact. At `dynamic_management.py` section `class DetectorDiagnosis:` the class body contains only annotated attributes plus `field(default_factory=dict)`, but unlike `FailureRecord` and `ModelResponse` it is missing `@dataclass`. Every call site in `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()`, `record_model_round()`, `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`, `self_diagnose()`, and `check_dispatch_health()` instantiates it as `DetectorDiagnosis(detector=..., pathology=..., ...)`. In Python, a plain class with annotations but no `__init__` will raise `TypeError: DetectorDiagnosis() takes no arguments`. This is independently observable from the code shape alone.  
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX:
<<<<
class DetectorDiagnosis:
    """Diagnosis from the detector health monitor."""
    detector: str  # "kappa", "mu", "d_decay"
    pathology: str  # human-readable description
    severity: str  # "WARNING", "CRITICAL"
    recommended_action: str  # what to do about it
    evidence: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # IM_F013: Machine-readable key for remediation routing, decoupled from
    # human-readable pathology string. Must match _REMEDIATION_CHAINS keys.
    pathology_key: str = ""
>>>>
====
@dataclass
class DetectorDiagnosis:
    """Diagnosis from the detector health monitor."""
    detector: str  # "kappa", "mu", "d_decay"
    pathology: str  # human-readable description
    severity: str  # "WARNING", "CRITICAL"
    recommended_action: str  # what to do about it
    evidence: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # IM_F013: Machine-readable key for remediation routing, decoupled from
    # human-readable pathology string. Must match _REMEDIATION_CHAINS keys.
    pathology_key: str = ""
>>>>
FOLLOW: This change affects every constructor call to `DetectorDiagnosis` across `record_round()`, `record_model_round()`, `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`, `self_diagnose()`, and `check_dispatch_health()`, all of which then become valid. No downstream code shown relies on identity, hashing, or mutability semantics that would be broken by dataclass conversion. No downstream impact identified beyond restoring constructibility.  
VERIFIED: TRUE


FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` records a `FailureRecord` before the effective recovery action is finalized, so persisted history can disagree with the action actually returned and executed. Location: `dynamic_management.py`, `FailureHandler.get_recovery()`. Evidence from the shown code: after deriving `action`, it immediately calls `self._record_failure(model_id, round_idx, failure_type, action)`. Only after that, in the execution block, it mutates behavior for `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`: if `current_role == Role.PAR`, it discards the model and rewrites `action = RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE`. The returned action is `EXCLUDE`, the active set is updated as exclusion, but the stored `FailureRecord.recovery_action` remains `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`. This is broader than the already-known PM/PAR downgrade-path issue because it corrupts the failure audit trail and any logic reading history.  
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX:
<<<<
        self._record_failure(model_id, round_idx, failure_type, action)

        # Execute exclusion if needed
        if action == RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE:
            self._active_models.discard(model_id)
        # IM_F008: Execute role downgrade — update role_map so subsequent
        # _expected_performance() calls use the correct baseline vector.
        elif action == RecoveryAction.DOWNGRADE_ROLE:
            current_role = self.role_map.get(model_id)
            if current_role == Role.COL:
                self.role_map[model_id] = Role.PAR
            elif current_role == Role.PAR:
                # Run 6 bug 6: PAR has no lower role. Escalate to EXCLUDE
                # instead of silently doing nothing.
                self._active_models.discard(model_id)
                action = RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE

        return action
>>>>
====
        # Finalise executable action before persisting it.
        if action == RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE:
            self._active_models.discard(model_id)
        elif action == RecoveryAction.DOWNGRADE_ROLE:
            current_role = self.role_map.get(model_id)
            if current_role == Role.COL:
                self.role_map[model_id] = Role.PAR
            elif current_role == Role.PAR:
                self._active_models.discard(model_id)
                action = RecoveryAction.EXCLUDE

        self._record_failure(model_id, round_idx, failure_type, action)
        return action
>>>>
FOLLOW: Any consumers of `get_failure_history()` will now see the actual executed action, not the pre-adjustment placeholder. This also aligns retry/escalation analytics with operational state changes. The PM hard-failure branch already records after action finalization and needs no change. No new inconsistency introduced.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` returns `FailureType.UNDERPERFORM` without emitting any corresponding manager event, while all higher-priority failure modes emit `ManagerEvent`s. Location: `dynamic_management.py`, `FailureHandler.detect_failure()`. Evidence: EMPTY/TIMEOUT/MALFORMED/FORMAT each call `_emit_event(...)` immediately before returning. The UNDERPERFORM branch directly returns `FailureType.UNDERPERFORM` after evaluating `underperform_count / len(recent_perfs) >= self.config.eta_underperform`, with no `_emit_event` call. This leaves the real-time PM monitoring stream incomplete for one of the documented failure types and creates an observability gap inside the immune/failure layer. This finding is distinct from the known FORMAT event-type misclassification; here the issue is missing event emission altogether for UNDERPERFORM.  
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX:
<<<<
        h = self.config.persistence_window
        recent_perfs = self._perf_history[response.model_id][-h:]
        if len(recent_perfs) >= h:
            underperform_count = sum(
                1 for p in recent_perfs if p < self.config.theta_under
            )
            if underperform_count / len(recent_perfs) >= self.config.eta_underperform:
                return FailureType.UNDERPERFORM
>>>>
====
        h = self.config.persistence_window
        recent_perfs = self._perf_history[response.model_id][-h:]
        if len(recent_perfs) >= h:
            underperform_count = sum(
                1 for p in recent_perfs if p < self.config.theta_under
            )
            if underperform_count / len(recent_perfs) >= self.config.eta_underperform:
                self._emit_event(
                    ManagerEvent(
                        event_type=ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM,
                        model_id=response.model_id,
                        round_idx=response.round_idx,
                        detail=(
                            f"Performance {perf:.3f} below threshold "
                            f"{self.config.theta_under:.3f} in "

FOLLOW: This requires `ManagerEventType` to define `UNDERPERFORM`. That enum body is skeletal in the artifact, so if the enum currently lacks that member, it must be added there as well. No other shown logic depends on underperformance being silent, so this is an observability-only correction with low behavioral risk.

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `check_dispatch_health()` bypasses the same-round remediation verification and self-diagnosis pipeline because it appends diagnoses directly to `self._diagnoses` after `record_round()` has already run. Location: `dynamic_management.py`, `DetectorHealthMonitor.check_dispatch_health()`. Evidence from the shown control responsibilities: `record_round()` is the only place that invokes `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` and `self_diagnose()`, and both operate before `self._diagnoses.extend(new_diagnoses)` for that round. `check_dispatch_health()` separately does `self._diagnoses.extend(new_diagnoses)` and returns. Therefore dispatch/verification diagnoses created after `record_round()` are invisible to the current round's `false_positive_rate`, remediation bookkeeping, and self-diagnosis trigger logic until at least the next round. A prior finding noted direct append as an ordering fragility in general, but the missed defect here is the concrete same-round omission for self-diagnosis metrics caused by the split entrypoint design.  
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX:
<<<<
        self._diagnoses.extend(new_diagnoses)
        return new_diagnoses
>>>>
====
        return new_diagnoses
>>>>

And in the caller integration path, merge these diagnoses before `record_round()` self-assessment work, e.g.:
<<<<
dispatch_diags = health_monitor.check_dispatch_health(
    dispatch_blocks, dispatch_successes, verification_rates, round_idx
)
>>>>
====
dispatch_diags = health_monitor.check_dispatch_health(
    dispatch_blocks, dispatch_successes, verification_rates, round_idx
)
health_monitor.register_diagnoses(dispatch_diags)
>>>>
FOLLOW: This fix moves ownership of diagnosis registration back to the orchestrator, consistent with `record_model_round()` and `register_diagnoses()`. Downstream consequence: call ordering in `process_round()` now matters explicitly; dispatch-health diagnoses must be registered before `record_round()` if they are meant to influence same-round `false_positive_rate` and self-diagnosis. If the integration currently calls `check_dispatch_health()` after `record_round()`, that ordering must also be corrected; the artifact does not show `process_round()`, so that adjacent code needs review.  
VERIFIED: TRUE


FINDING_ID: IM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` can raise `KeyError` for dynamically added models because `_perf_history` is indexed directly after only conditionally appending via `setdefault`. Location: `dynamic_management.py`, `FailureHandler.detect_failure()`. Evidence: the append path uses `self._perf_history.setdefault(response.model_id, []).append(perf)`, but the later read is unconditional: `recent_perfs = self._perf_history[response.model_id][-h:]`. If a duplicate callback arrives for a model/round key already present in `_perf_rounds_seen` before `_perf_history` has been initialized for that `model_id` in this process instance, the append block is skipped and the direct index raises. This is reachable for dynamic model addition or partial state restoration, both explicitly plausible in this subsystem.  
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX:
<<<<
        h = self.config.persistence_window
        recent_perfs = self._perf_history[response.model_id][-h:]
>>>>
====
        h = self.config.persistence_window
        recent_perfs = self._perf_history.setdefault(response.model_id, [])[-h:]
>>>>
FOLLOW: This aligns the read path with the write path and removes a hidden dependency on constructor-time model enumeration. The same dynamic-addition risk also exists for `_failure_history` and `self.models` access patterns elsewhere, but those are either already guarded with `.get()` or outside this specific crash path. No downstream impact identified.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_get_metric_history()` and `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` do not support the dispatch-health target metrics generated within the analytical boundary, so remediation verification for those pathologies cannot work even if chains exist. Location: `dynamic_management.py`, methods `_get_metric_history()` and `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`. Evidence: supported metrics are only `"kappa"`, `"mu"`, `"novelty"`, `"finding_count"`, and `"vocab_growth"`. But `check_dispatch_health()` emits pathologies `dispatch_false_positive` and `verification_miscalibration`; if `apply_diagnosis()` maps these to remediations with natural target metrics like `dispatch_false_positive`, `verification_rate`, or `verification_miscalibration`, the P-pass trend check sees empty history and outcome verification silently `continue`s forever. A prior known finding covered several unsupported names, but it did not include `verification_rate`/`verification_miscalibration` history derivation from the shown dispatch-health state.

FINDING_ID: IM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.56  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `self_diagnose()` enforces one global damping timer for all self-adjustment triggers, so an adjustment for one trigger suppresses independent adjustments for other triggers in subsequent rounds. Location: `dynamic_management.py`, `DetectorHealthMonitor.self_diagnose()`. Evidence: the method checks only `self._last_self_adjust_round`; if `current_round - self._last_self_adjust_round < damping_rounds`, it returns immediately before evaluating any of the three self-checks. This means, for example, a legitimate high `false_positive_rate` can be ignored just because a low-remediation-success adjustment was applied recently. The config text says `immune_damping_rounds` is the minimum rounds between adjustments to the same parameter, not a global mute on all self-corrections.  
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX:
<<<<
        if hasattr(self, '_last_self_adjust_round'):
            if current_round - self._last_self_adjust_round < damping_rounds:
                return diagnoses  # Damping: skip self-adjustment this round
>>>>
====
        if not hasattr(self, "_last_self_adjust_rounds"):
            self._last_self_adjust_rounds = {}
>>>>

Then gate each trigger independently, for example in Self-check 1:
<<<<
        if len(self._remediation_outcomes) >= 3 and success_rate < 0.3:
>>>>
====
        if (
            len(self._remediation_outcomes) >= 3
            and success_rate < 0.3
            and current_round - self._last_self_adjust_rounds.get(
                "low_remediation_success_rate", -10**9
            ) >= damping_rounds
        ):
>>>>

And update writes similarly:
<<<<
                        self._last_self_adjust_round = current_round  # SD-2
>>>>
====
                        self._last_self_adjust_rounds["low_remediation_success_rate"] = current_round
>>>>

For Self-check 2:
<<<<
        if len(self._false_positive_history) >= 2 and fp_rate > 0.5:
>>>>
====
        if (
            len(self._false_positive_history) >= 2
            and fp_rate > 0.5
            and current_round - self._last_self_adjust_rounds.get(
                "high_false_positive_rate", -10**9
            ) >= damping_rounds
        ):
>>>>

And its write:
<<<<
                    self._last_self_adjust_round = current_round  # SD-2
>>>>
====
                    self._last_self_adjust_rounds["high_false_positive_rate"] = current_round
>>>>
FOLLOW: `__init__` should initialize `self._last_self_adjust_rounds: Dict[str, int] = {}` for structural consistency rather than dynamic creation. This change allows concurrent but parameter-disjoint self-corrections while preserving per-trigger hysteresis. No shown code reads `_last_self_adjust_round` elsewhere, so replacing it is safe within boundary.  
VERIFIED: TRUE


FINDING_ID: IM_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.51  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.36  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The documentation in `record_round()` is materially inaccurate about return semantics versus side effects. Location: `dynamic_management.py`, `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` docstring. Evidence: the docstring states only “Returns: List of new diagnoses (may be empty if detectors are healthy).” In reality the method also mutates internal state by appending histories, invoking `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`, invoking `self_diagnose()`, and extending `self._diagnoses` with all resulting diagnoses. This matters because the subsystem already has mixed ownership between `record_round()`, `record_model_round()`, and `check_dispatch_health()`, and the hidden append side effect is part of the integration fragility. This is not the same as the known asymmetry finding for `record_model_round()`; this is specifically the inaccurate contract text on the main entrypoint.  
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX:
<<<<
        Returns:
            List of new diagnoses (may be empty if detectors are healthy).
>>>>
====
        Returns:
            List of new diagnoses for this round.

        Side effects:
            - Appends detector metric histories.
            - Verifies pending remediation outcomes.
            - Runs self_diagnosis checks.
            - Appends all diagnoses produced here to self._diagnoses.
            External diagnoses from record_model_round() / check_dispatch_health()
            must be registered separately via register_diagnoses() if they should
            participate in monitor-level accounting.
>>>>
FOLLOW: This documentation fix does not alter runtime behavior, but it exposes the required ownership boundary and makes the integration issue in `process_round()` auditable. No downstream code impact.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
